before.answer:
**Meaning**  
`ERR-PO-0412` displays `TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (<state>)` [1]. It is raised by `po_save` on screen `PUR-PO-01` when a purchase order line tax code does not match the country recorded on the supplier master account [1][2]. This occurs primarily because Ledgerline defaults domestic code `VAT20-UK` even for non-UK vendors [1][3].

**How to fix**  
1. Verify the supplier’s recorded country [1].  
2. Amend the line tax code:  
   - For suppliers outside the UK, change the code to `VAT20-RC` for standard goods or `VAT5-RC` for reduced-rate items [1][3].  
   - For UK suppliers, ensure it is set to `VAT20-UK` [1].  
3. Keep the cursor in the line details area and press `F8` to save and recommit the order [1].  

If the error recurs frequently for a vendor, notify the purchase ledger team to update the supplier master profile [1].

after.answer:
**Meaning**
`ERR-PO-0412` displays the message `TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (<state>)` [1] (or `[<country_code>]` [2]). It indicates that the tax code entered on a purchase order does not match the supplier country recorded on the supplier's master account (for example, applying a UK code to an overseas vendor or vice versa) [1][2].

**How to fix**
1. Check the supplier's recorded country [1].
2. On screen `PUR-PO-01`, amend the line tax code to match the supplier location [1]:
   - **Suppliers outside the UK:** Change to reverse-charge code `VAT20-RC` for standard goods or `VAT5-RC` for reduced-rate items [1].
   - **UK suppliers:** Set to `VAT20-UK` [1].
3. Keep the cursor in the line details area and press **F8** to save [1].

Never force domestic codes for overseas suppliers; if occurrences are frequent, contact the purchase ledger team to correct the supplier master profile [1].

source_text.title: Ledgerline ERP 7.2.3-P6 Patch Notes
source_text.summary: Ledgerline ERP 7.2.3-P6 was released on 23 October 2026 and installed at Northbridge Cycles on 26 October 2026 at 07:00 (change CR-2026-034). It changes how Fetch fills the tax code and adds a blocking setting to the certificate check introduced in 7.2.3-P4.
changes: Fetch (F3, service po_fetch) now fills the tax code from the supplier's country: VAT20-UK for a supplier in GB, VAT20-RC for a supplier in any other country. Before this patch Fetch always filled VAT20-UK, which caused ERR-PO-0412 for overseas suppliers. Orders saved before the patch are not changed.

Parameter PUR.CERT_CHK accepts a third value, B (block). With B, Save on PUR-PO-01 of an order for an item with the lithium-cell flag is refused with ERR-SUP-0208 UN38.3 CERTIFICATE MISSING OR EXPIRED when the supplier has no UN38.3 certificate valid on the order date. Y still only warns (W-SUP-0207). The default stays N.
The certificate check still looks only at the valid-to date. It does not apply company rules on issue dates or margins.
source_text.effect: At Northbridge, PUR.CERT_CHK stays N: the change board decided on 7 October 2026 (CR-2026-031) to review the certificate check in January 2027. The manual check in SOP-PUR-001 remains the control. The new Fetch behaviour is live from 26 October 2026: buyers no longer need to change VAT20-UK to VAT20-RC by hand for overseas suppliers, but should still check the tax code before Save.
